Brandon Beack

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
He thought he would never be able to compete gain but Brandon's determination not only helped himself but is helping others

Summary:
.Brandon Beake, a top athlete and gymnast, with his national colours broke his back and spine in a gymnastic accident at school. He was paralysed, to all intents and purpose, a quadriplegic
.
But Brandon and his family were determined not to give up. Through intensive rehabilitation, iron-will and hard work he has not only regained use of his arms but is now competing internationally at Olympic level in a number of disciplines. He has set a new South African and African record for the Men's 100m wheelchair sprints
But that’s probably not the most impressive thing about Brandon Beake, he was able to afford (with medical aid help) extensive rehabilitation at one of the best centres in the world in Atlanta Georgia – where Christopher Reeve went -and came back determined to help less fortunate South Africans.




Further information:
Brandon has set up the first of its kind Neurological Rehabilitation Centre in Cape Town, together with his NPO, ‘Walking with Brandon’ he is aiming to give disadvantaged people access to this rehab. In Khayelitsha he has paired up with Dube, who has been through his programme and now they are helping others. They on the way to making this rehab super world class, on the lines of Christopher Reeve’s facility but with access to all.

Brandon was nominated as one of SA’s top 200 South Africans.

Other Facts:

1. From an effective state of quadriplegia after his gymnastic accident, Brandon has restored not only the use of his arms but has now set a new South African and African record for the Men's 100m wheelchair sprints
2. Set a new South African record for Men's Shot Put.
3. Done a number of motivational talks at Schools around the Western Cape, as well as spoke at Stellenbosch University.
4. Achieved Rio qualifying times and distances for Shot Put and 100m sprints
5. Competed at the IWAS U23 World Games in Prague and achieved GOLD for Shot Put and 4th place for 100m sprints.
6. Set up the first of its kind in South Africa, Neurological Rehabilitation Centre in Cape.

Summary: Brandon Beack, a top athlete and gymnast, with national colours, broke his back and spine in a gymnastic accident at school. He was paralysed - to all intents and purpose, a quadriplegic. But Brandon and his family were determined not to give up.

Script:


Brandon: 90% battle won if you have a good mind set as Will Smith said once I have made that decision its already been done I am just waiting for the rest of the world to see it ….

V/O 12 sec
Four years ago 16 year old Brandon Beack, had his whole life set out, a dancer, a gymnast with his national colours and a dream to compete in the Olympics and then….

Brandon: I was Training for Western Province trials, I did a dismount on the side of the parallel bars something went wrong I think my technique was out but I ended up landing on my head missing the safety mat split my head open

Annette: Arriving at the gymnastics club Brandon was lying on floor and his head had a huge gash I was immediately thinking brain damage

Mark: I saw there was a lot of blood around him, I checked his vitals very stable, responsive started feeling cant feel his body pinch down shoulder… lot more serious than it appears

Brandon: My spinal chord ended up in an s and was compressed from 14 mm to 2mm.

Link: Brandon badly damaged his C6 C7 vertebrae suffering a complete spinal cord injury he was confined to a wheel chair and told he would never walk again a quadriplegic.

Brandon: When Dr told me my parents took it very hard, I cut it out at that moment because something inside me said No…to me that wasn’t my future

Annette : We were told we have stop living in denial accept Brandon’s fate. At that stage he was complete quad no hand function couldn’t feed dress himself couldn’t brush his teeth couldn’t get it wrapped around my mind set that this is it couldn’t be.

V/O 17 sec
Not accepting this fate, Annette and Mark began looking at alternative options, for their son. They sold their house, worked two jobs and fund raised to send Brandon to the Shepherd Centre in Atlanta, United States for 6 weeks of state of the art rehabilitaion.

Brandon: The SC was heck of an experience no matter how badly injured/disabled you are there always mind set you can recover that you will only get good results if you put the effort.
John: So in the States they were feeding your mental state of mind which is obviously important as part of the rehabilitation process?
Brandon: In the end all come down to you mentally making connection with the muscle you might not feel it but just visualise it moving that muscle over time that repetitive visualisation that repetitive move will start connecting

V/O 11 sec
Brandon returned home having regained most of the use of his arms. He started training with Rob Evans. The game changer was the robotic suit, the Beack’s had brought back.

Rob: Something like the robotic suit really does help
..It would be impossible to get someone upright and walking, that type of smoothness without that type of technologies.

Brandon: Rob helped me get through lowest times taught how to focus psychologically. I had a mind set of just doing therapy and he said you are stronger than you think lets do sports.
John: Was he responsible Para Olympic direction
Brandon: Yes, that was him because of 2 people the second person who played quiet a big role is Acmid Hassim, Shark boy …..friends mentor the moment he saw me egging me on ……

Link: With the support of his parents Brandon has help equip this centre the SSC I in CT through his WWBF he s paying it forward providing therapy to people who otherwise couldn’t afford it.

V/O 13 sec
Therapy and Beyond is the result, still in its early stages they aim for a rehabilitation centre for people who would not normally have access to intensive and extensive rehabilitation’

Brandon: I was offered an hour a week that’s a maintenance programme you are not going to recover from that.
Rob: So Brandon experienced that and that’s where idea came in we do need to take beyond that phase…..
John: You want to offer people chance to have that therapy despite their financial circumstance
Mark: they don’t have to fund it they don’t have pay they will be able to get it through the foundation

V/O 7 sec
Last year Msingathi Dube, who is paralysed from the waist down, started with Therapy and Beyond.

LINK: In 2010 SA was basking in the glory of hosting the Soccer WWC but for Msingathi Dube what should have been a time of celebration became a desperate fight for his life….as he and 2 and t others were caught in the crossfire of a bitter Khayileitsha gang feud.

Dube : I remember waking up in the hospital but I cant feel my legs I think you are paralysed from the chest down so I would never be able to walk again.
John: That’s a difficult thing to hear
Dube: It is, if you could see that Dr’s face when he was telling me…

John: How did meeting with Brandon change your life?
Dube: He motivated me he is trying to change my life…he trained me its not going to be easy but we are going to get there.

V/O 10 sec
Msingathi’s been training in the suit for the past 5 months, he can now take 1500 steps and stand for two hours in it, great progress

John: And the first time you took first step in that suit?
Dube: Amazing because after so many years you start walking again it gives you much hope.

V/O 16 sec
Only four years after his life changing accident Brandon has set a new South African and African record for the Men's 100m wheelchair sprints, and while he qualified for this years Para- Olympics , due to team size he couldn’t go,,,,
Brandon: I had goal for Rio sadly not on the team but I qualified…that’s what I wanted to do in year I could qualify so next up 2020 if I am not walking by then.

Annette: ….it took me a long time to understand when B would be ok….emotional saw B take part in disabled sports event he was shining I tough he is going to be ok now… …

Brandon: My end goal is to walk and in the meantime I might as well take the opportunity of being in a wheel chair and get involved in sports and train for para enjoy my time because its opened up new opportunities for me that I wouldn’t have had before injury so why dwell on negative on what I cant do. I cant walk I can’t use my legs that’s the only difference… I can do just as much as you can.
